# FDG8023

> CONSIDER using subclasses of generic base collections instead of using the collections directly.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 8.3.2 Collection Properties and Return Values.

## How it is checked

- Check: judgment
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library suggestion, application suggestion, test none
- Status: verified

Test profile: test classes are public only for the test framework; their signatures are not API. Not machine-checkable: whether a better name or helper members are worth a subclass is judgment; the text applies it especially to high-level APIs.

## From the book

This allows for a better name and for adding helper members that are not present on the base collection types. This is especially applicable to high-level APIs.

```csharp
public TraceSourceCollection : Collection<TraceSource> {
  // optional helper method
  public void FlushAll {
    foreach(TraceSource source in this){
      source.Flush();
   }
  }
  // another common helper
  public void AddSource(string sourceName){
    Add(new TraceSource(sourceName));
  }
}
```
